original_target.title: Full interior regularity for the nondegenerate symmetric p-Laplace system

full_original_statement:
Let $`n\ge3`$, $`1<p<\infty`$, $`p\ne2`$, and let $`B_1\subset\mathbb R^n`$ be the open unit ball. For $`u\in W^{1,p}(B_1;\mathbb R^n)`$ write

```math
e(u)=\frac{\nabla u+\nabla u^{\mathsf T}}2,
\qquad A(P)=(1+|P|^2)^{(p-2)/2}P,
```

where $`|P|`$ is the Frobenius norm. Suppose $`u`$ solves the homogeneous system weakly:

```math
\int_{B_1} A(e(u)):e(\varphi)\,dx=0
\quad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(B_1;\mathbb R^n).
```

Is every such $`u`$ of class $`C^{1,\alpha}_{\mathrm{loc}}(B_1;\mathbb R^n)`$ for some $`\alpha\in(0,1)`$? Prove this assertion, or produce an admissible weak solution for which it fails. No boundary condition, pressure, or divergence-free constraint is imposed.

sources.scope_comparison: The actual theorem obtains W1,2 local regularity of the nonlinear stress for p in (p−(n),p+(n)); the following text extends this to the exact nondegenerate Carreau law nu=1. This is Sobolev stress regularity, not C1,alpha of every weak solution in all n>=3 and all p≠2. The introduction explicitly retains full higher-dimensional Holder-gradient regularity as an open problem. Full-gradient p-Laplace and pressure-constrained p-Stokes results change the equation.
